points.name: apps.alarm.list.row_register
points.interpretation: List update and row creation register the entry-defined callback with filter 7 and the current row index as user data. Alarm rows normally select 0x0c53d689; the add row uses another callback.

points.name: apps.alarm.list.switch_register
points.interpretation: List update and row creation register callback 0x0c53d405 with filter 30 and row index as user data.

points.name: apps.alarm.list.row_event_code
points.interpretation: The existing-alarm row callback only enters its edit/navigation branch when event code equals 7.

points.name: apps.alarm.list.row_index
points.interpretation: The existing-alarm row callback resolves this value to an alarm record, copies the record into the editor state, then navigates to the edit page.

points.name: apps.alarm.list.switch_event_code
points.interpretation: The switch callback resolves the row index first and writes the switched state into the UI and alarm record only for event code 30.

points.name: apps.alarm.list.switch_index
points.interpretation: The switch callback resolves the index before its event-code check and uses it to index a 28-byte UI row; an invalid index may corrupt memory.

evidence: The main-page lifecycle allocates and publishes its state, freeing it and clearing the slot on destroy. The list builder puts the existing-alarm callback into each row record; row create/update register that record callback with filter 7 and row index. Switch create/update register the state-change callback with filter 30 and row index. Handler disassembly establishes the event tests, alarm resolution and record writes.
scope: Only the listed creation/update registration call sites and two individual callbacks; other alarm management paths are not covered.
limitations: The index must address a valid current alarm row; overriding it with an out-of-range value can cause invalid memory access. Suppressing or rewriting an operation can leave visual and saved state inconsistent. The page state and root slots do not stop concurrent threads; publication and rollback of shared entry patches require system-wide quiescence. Device behavior remains unverified.
